children: have signed a strategic cooperation agreement to expand U.S. production of solid rocket motors, a critical component of guided missiles. The agreement is intended to increase manufacturing capacity and diversify the supply chain as demand for military munitions rises.

The initial collaboration will focus on rocket motors for Lockheed Martin's Extended Range Guided Multiple Launch Rocket System, or ER GMLRS, and Precision Strike Missile, or PrSM. Production will take place at a new Avio USA facility under construction in Hurt, Virginia, following completion of the required qualification process.
For investors, the agreement could help Lockheed

address supply constraints that limit its ability to increase missile production and fulfill defense orders. Additional rocket motor capacity could support higher manufacturing volumes and revenue growth, particularly as the U.S. military and allied governments replenish weapons inventories. For Avio

, the agreement establishes a potential source of demand for its planned U.S. manufacturing operations, though neither company disclosed production volumes, contract values or a timetable for deliveries.
Solid rocket motors provide propulsion for tactical missiles and have become an important supply-chain consideration as defense contractors seek to increase output. Under the agreement, Lockheed
will gain access to a portion of Avio's production capacity, potentially reducing its dependence on existing suppliers and providing greater flexibility in meeting customer requirements.

Tim Cahill, president of Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control, said diversifying rocket motor suppliers is central to the company's efforts to expand missile production. The agreement is expected to help Lockheed Martin respond to growing demand while reducing the risk of manufacturing disruptions.

has committed more than $500 million to developing solid rocket motor production capacity in the United States. Giulio Ranzo, chief executive officer of Avio, said the investment is intended to establish the company as a supplier to multiple defense customers. James Syring, CEO of Avio USA, said the Lockheed
programs would help establish a production base for the Virginia factory as the company continues construction and workforce recruitment.

The agreement comes as defense manufacturers face pressure to increase missile output amid heightened military spending and efforts to rebuild ammunition stockpiles. Its financial impact will depend on the Virginia facility's construction progress, successful qualification of its rocket motors and the volume of future orders.

title: Lockheed Martin, Avio agree to expand U.S. rocket motor production
